ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, on the left is a sinusoidal AC power source labeled Vs, and the input current is is marked; in the middle, four thyristors/SCRs with gate symbols form a single-phase fully controlled bridge; on the right, an inductor and a load are connected, indicating that the bridge-type fully controlled rectifier supplies power to a highly inductive DC load. Reasoning: The problem states that the load current has no ripple, so the DC current Id can be considered continuous and constant. For a single-phase fully controlled bridge under continuous current, viewed from the AC side, the input current is is a rectangular wave with amplitude ±Id, conducting for 180° each half cycle, and delayed by the firing angle α relative to the fundamental wave of the source voltage. The total RMS value of this rectangular current is Is,rms = Id, and the fundamental RMS value is I1,rms = 2√2 Id/π, so the distortion factor is I1,rms/Is,rms = 2√2/π ≈ 0.9003. The fundamental displacement factor is cos α = cos 30° ≈ 0.866. Input power factor = distortion factor × displacement factor = (2√2/π)cos30° ≈ 0.9003 × 0.866 ≈ 0.78.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a full-wave controlled bridge feeding a DC load through an inductor. From the text take α = 30° and constant load current Id. Let the supply peak be Vm.
